cards.title: AI4AI-Bench发布：首个评估AI自我改进能力的基准测试

entities.name: AI4AI-Bench
entities.explain: 一个用于测试AI系统能否改进自身训练算法的基准测试平台

entities.name: 递归自我改进(RSI)
entities.explain: AI系统改进产生自己的训练过程，使下一代系统继承改进的能力

cards.summary: AI4AI-Bench是首个专门评估大语言模型代理在算法设计中进行递归自我改进能力的基准测试。该基准测试关注AI系统能否优化自身的训练算法，从而让下一代系统继承改进。这为衡量AI自我进化能力提供了标准化方法。
cards.relevant: 递归自我改进是通向通用人工智能的关键路径，该基准测试为评估这一能力提供了重要工具。
cards.source_text: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement。Recursive self-improvement (RSI) asks whether an AI system can improve the process that produces AI systems, so that the next system inherits the improvement. That process is the training algorithm: a better objective or update rule improves the compute\mbox{-}capability exchange rate for every subs
cards.source_title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement

cards.title: ConceptGuard发布：首个评估大语言模型上下文敏感遗忘能力的基准

entities.name: ConceptGuard
entities.explain: 一个用于测试大语言模型能否在特定上下文中选择性遗忘知识的基准测试

entities.name: 大语言模型遗忘
entities.explain: 从AI模型中移除有害或敏感知识的技术，类似人类选择性遗忘

cards.summary: ConceptGuard是首个评估大语言模型上下文敏感遗忘能力的基准测试。现有方法依赖不相交的遗忘和保留数据集，无法全面评估这一能力。ConceptGuard填补了这一空白，为AI安全研究提供了更完整的评估框架。
cards.relevant: 随着AI模型规模扩大，如何安全移除有害知识成为关键安全问题，该基准为这一领域提供了重要评估工具。
cards.source_text: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models。Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly require selective removal of harmful or sensitive knowledge, called unlearning, yet existing methods and benchmarks fail to evaluate this capability completely. cards.source_title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models

cards.relevant: 医疗AI的可解释性对临床决策至关重要，该研究推动了可解释医疗AI的发展。

cards.relevant: 为音乐信息检索系统提供了更可靠的置信度评估，提升AI系统的可信度。

entities.explain: 调频连续波雷达，通过发射连续调频信号探测目标

entities.name: IR-UWB
entities.explain: 脉冲无线电超宽带，通过极短脉冲信号进行高精度测距

entities.name: Wi-Fi感知
entities.explain: 利用Wi-Fi信号变化检测人体活动的技术

cards.relevant: 无接触式健康监测是智慧医疗的重要方向，该对比研究为实际应用提供了技术选择依据。

items.title: ezfe 在「AI companies destroy physical books – le」下的评论
items.summary: I dislike these AI companies but let's be clear here: the copyright holders are the ones locking these books up. If they don't want to print more copies, then they could release the copyright on them. Instead, they enforce the copyright and force AI companies to shred books they want to ingest. edit: Also, an AI company would only ever care to purchase, scan, destroy a book once. Presumably many books have more than one copy.

items.summary: The piracy organizations are playing 4D chess while everyone else is playing checkers. The irony of this entire situation - AI companies being legally required to shred books due to kafkaesque copyright laws, then used as a marketing tactic by Anna's Archive - is a work of art. I support Anna's Archive, by the way. Information wants to be free.
items.author: HedonicEscal8r

items.title: shakna 在「AI companies destroy physical books – le」下的评论
items.summary: I wholeheartedly believe the AI controversy on destroying books is being stirred up by the companies themselves. Copyright law requires you destroy a book, if you format shift it. If you digitise, you need to ensure its not a "copy" but that your one license went with the book. So... If enough people complain, they get to pressure for copyright changes. Which will just so happen to have massive carveouts to let them do whatever they want.
